newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt approves NZ$4 mln rise in CAA budget.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt approves NZ$4 mln rise in CAA budget.

text.p: The New Zealand government has approved a NZ$4 million increase in the Civil Aviation Authority's budget, to NZ$17.75 million, the CAA said on Thursday.
The revised funding system will apply from July 11.
"The funding will provide resources critical to the CAA meeting its aviation safety tasks as well as responding to substantial industry growth," the CAA said.
The new funding package includes a rise in the Domestic Passenger Levy to NZ$2.15 per trip from $1.80. This is the primary source of CAA funding and will raise $9.56 million.

The package introduces a departing international passenger levy of $1 per person, but the current international passenger security charge paid to the Aviation Security Service will be cut by the same amount, for a nil effect on passengers.
This will raise $2.58 million for the CAA.
Some fees and charges are increased and some reduced, raising a further $2.46 million.
The CAA said the government was considering a capital injection of $1 million as part of its 1997/98 budget, to counter an urgent need to improve capital and taxpayers' equity.
It said the approved funding package would allow CAA staffing to rise to 148 from 120.
